items.summaryOriginal:
Learn how the latest Android Studio AI features can streamline your daily development tasks. While the original agent mode chat was helpful, we rebuilt it with a re-architected experience that supports parallel tool calls and background sub-agents. For instance, you can now have an agent analyze code in the background while you continue working on a different feature. Try out the updated Journeys feature to see how plain text instructions can automatically test your critical user paths.

items.summary:
人工智能可以因为错误的原因做正确的事吗？ Tim Scarfe 与 Apollo Research 的 Alexander Meinke、Axel Højmark 和 Jérémy Scheurer 讨论了通过对比信念更新衡量奖励寻求，这是他们与 OpenAI 合作的新研究。

items.summaryOriginal:
Can an AI do the right thing for the wrong reason? Tim Scarfe speaks with Apollo Research’s Alexander Meinke, Axel Højmark and Jérémy Scheurer about Measuring Reward-Seeking via Contrastive Belief Updates, their new research with OpenAI.

The panel asks how models infer what graders reward, why good behaviour can come from the wrong reason, and whether that difference can be measured. The conversation moves through promise-breaking, grader awareness, reward hacking, scheming, opaque reasoning and corrigibility, then turns to a detailed walkthrough of the contrastive-belief method and what its results do and do not show. items.titleZh: 看着美国与人工智能失控——Alistair Pullen (Cosine AI)
items.summary:
本集由 Notion 赞助。 Learn more about Notion's Developer Platform today at https://notion.com/mlst

Britain's most capable coding model can't be exported, and that ban is the whole reason Cosine set out to build one from scratch. Cosine 首席执行官兼联合创始人阿利斯泰尔·普伦 (Alistair Pullen) 与蒂姆·斯卡夫 (Tim Scarfe) 坐下来解释了一个被他称为 Fable 的前沿系统（被锁定在美国出口管制之下）如何成为在布里斯托尔的 Isambard 超级计算机上训练的英国主权模型的创始案例。

其背后的赌注是经济的。普伦认为，一家推理公司，而不是一家以训练为先的实验室，不需要数十亿美元来竞争：数百万美元、国家计算分配和一个联盟……

items.titleOriginal: The Thermodynamic AI Chip · Thomas Ahle
items.titleZh: 热力学人工智能芯片 Thomas Ahle
items.summary:
Thomas Ahle 希望普通计算成为芯片设计的宠儿：输入您的意图，一群代理将其从设计、优化、形式化和验证到流片。为了实现这一目标，他的团队编写了自己的开源 Verilog 模拟器，在 43 天内编写了 580,000 行代码，因为商业 EDA 验证器每个内核的运行成本约为 10,000 美元，而且没有像样的开源编译器可供构建。

这就提出了蒂姆一直在追问的问题：如果一个代理人可以生产出芯片设计、证明或工作程序，你如何知道它是正确的？通过 70% 的测试并不等于正确，一个捏造的错误可能会让公司损失惨重。他们深入P...
items.summaryOriginal:
Thomas Ahle wants Normal Computing to be the Lovable for chip design: type your intent, and a swarm of agents carries it from design through optimisation, formalisation and verification to tape-out. To get there, his team at wrote their own open-source Verilog simulator, 580,000 lines in 43 days, because commercial EDA verifiers run about $10,000 per core and there are no decent open-source compilers to build on.

That sets up the question Tim keeps pressing: if an agent can produce a chip design, a proof, or a working program, how do you actually know it is correct? Passing 70% of tests is not the same as being right, and a single fabricated bug can cost a company a fortune. They dig into P...
